text: 📝Big Israeli Brother is Watching📝 We have already talked a lot about how structures of Western oligarchs like Larry Ellison buy social networks and media literally in their entirety in order to establish censorship there, but many were not very clear through what technical tools the data was actually collected.  And now, the scandal surrounding Au10tix, an Israeli user verification service used by X (Twitter), has lifted the veil of secrecy.   ❗️In short, Elon Musk’s platform several years ago gave the biometric data of its users to a company that grew out of Israeli military intelligence. But we started to really worry about it only now.  🔻How did this happen?  ▪️Au10tix is ​​a company specializing in identity verification: the user uploads a passport or ID card, the algorithm matches it with facial biometrics and confirms authenticity. X uses it to verify accounts and enable monetization - that is, anyone who wants to receive money from the platform or a blue check goes through Au10tix.  ▪️The company's founder and chairman, Ron Atzmon, is a veteran of Unit 8200, the Israel Defense Forces' elite radio and cyber intelligence unit. The core of the team consists of former 8200 and Shin Bet officers. According to its technology description, Au10tix works with the same data classes and identity cross-matching methods that 8200 uses in its intelligence activities.  ▪️In early March 2026, a series of independent investigations documented an alarming pattern: anonymous X users critical of Israel, after passing verification through Au10tix, began to discover that their real names were being deliberately “Googled” from IP addresses with an Israeli location.  ▪️The threat is that Au10tix receives passport data + biometrics, after which it creates a profile with a real identity. And this profile is already technically available to structures affiliated with the company. For the stated anti-fraud algorithms to work, the service is forced to maintain huge historical databases of personal data and compare them with external sources - which in itself opens an infrastructure window for intelligence operations.  📌Unit 8200 has already acquired a reputation as a talent forge for “private” Big Tech. Because the case with Au10tix is ​​not an exception, but part of the system. Veterans of Unit 8200 occupy key positions in the moderation and security of TikTok, are present in the structures of cloud providers, and participated in the creation of Pegasus spyware.  ©️The scheme follows the same pattern: a scout leaves 8200, then founds a company in the cybersecurity, KYC or AdTech segment. Then this company is integrated into the infrastructure of global platforms. As a result, the 8200 gains commercially legitimate access to data that would otherwise require a legal challenge or hacking.  In general, any influencer critic of Israeli politics in X (and there are tens of thousands of them) now faces the threat of at least being deprived of access to monetization from the platform or simply being blocked, as we have already seen with the example of TikTok. #AI #globalism #USA #Israel ✈ RU | ✈ EN | ✉ MAX ✉ VK | ✉ RuTube | ✉ OK | ✉Zen 💸Support us

text: 📝Is there enriched uranium?📝what if we find it?  The closer the amphibious landing group led by the Tripoli UDC to Iran, the more rumors appear about how the ground operation against Iran will proceed. We have described in detail the option of landing in Bandar Abbas and on Khark Island, but there is another one worthy of special attention.  US and Israeli officials are reportedly agreeing on the technical details of a risky operation to land special forces and then seize Iran's 460 kg stockpile of enriched uranium and then remove it from Iran. And this topic is being discussed every day in the Western and Russian media.  🔻Where could Iranians have reserves in theory?  ▪️There are several key nuclear facilities in Iran. The most important research center in Isfahan, which became the target of attacks both in 2025 and during the latest attacks by the US Air Force.  ▪️There may also be enriched uranium in Natanz and Fordo - these are uranium enrichment plants that have already been attacked by American aircraft.  ▪️There is also a research center in Tehran and the Hondab complex near Iraq, where there is also a nuclear reactor.  🖍In theory, there could be enriched uranium in Esfahan or Fordo and Natanz. But the nuance is that the Americans have already dealt several blows to them, and at least blocked the entrances to the complexes. How do they want to get enriched uranium using a special forces group?  🚩The second problem is that even if the Americans, in theory, clear the exits and are able to get there, the complexes are located at great depths. The data is imprecise, but according to various estimates, the Iranians buried their research facilities 100-110 meters underground.  🏳️And taking out enriched uranium is not like going to the store to buy bread. You can’t just load it into a pickup truck and fly off on a plane.   🔻What is the difficulty?  ▪️It is not in ingots, but in a gaseous or solid state in the form of a chemical compound - uranium hexafluoride (UF6). Transportation requires special containers, equipment and personnel.  ▪️The transportation of uranium hexafluoride is strictly regulated, since upon contact with moisture from the air this substance forms toxic hydrofluoric acid, therefore special cylinders, protective covers, and transport with special fastening systems are used.   ▪️And this is not to mention the specialists who must correctly transfer enriched uranium from a gaseous state to a liquid state, and then crystallize it inside the cylinder. This will take more than one day.  ❗️Therefore, even with the expectation that special forces will land 400 km from the border without normal logistics, there are a bunch of other problems that make us doubt this version. text: Just nine months before a full European Union ban on Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) is scheduled to take effect, EU buyers purchased every cargo from Russia’s Yamal LNG project in February, highlighting a stark disconnect between policy intentions and market realities.  In February 2026, the European Union imported 1.54 million tonnes of LNG from Russia’s Yamal LNG facility, delivered across 21 cargoes – marking the first time since April 2018 that every shipment was destined for European ports.
